title: From an Imbedded Legal Lore to a Practical Reality
primary_topics: Closing address at the FLP Awards Ceremony, July 28, 2023 -- welcoming 21 new law scholars, 10 dissertation winners, and 5 ESMEL fellows
CJP's autobiographical 'imbedded legal lore to practical reality' narrative: how his judicial philosophy moved from the Court into the Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity
Two 'ultimate projects' of FLP: the Museum for Liberty and Prosperity (AI-powered, immersive, interactive) and the Prosperity Fund (multi-billion-peso MSME fund)
Life as 'a strange interplay of light and shadows' -- doors closed by poverty and visa denial opened larger windows; governing philosophy for the scholars

Ricardo Pilares III representing MVP who was at Maynilad); Ayala Corporation (Fernando Zobel de Ayala); Alfred and Cherry Ty (Metrobank Foundation, FLP Professorial Chairs); Msgr. Three Board of Judges chairs: Justice Amy C. Lazaro-Javier; Gov. Amando Tetangco Jr. (newly elected SM Investments Chair, first publicly-listed company with P1 trillion+ market cap); CJ Gesmundo

Special guests: Atty. Felipe Gozon (GMA Chairman and CEO -- CJP invited him to join the Court but Gozon preferred GMA; CJP has been an independent GMA director for 16 years since 2006); World Bank executives Dandan Chen and Dave Llorito (handpicked by Ndiame Diop); Injap Sia (declined attendance but donated P888,000 unsolicited); Marixi Rufino Prieto (donated three-fourths page colored FLP ad in the Inquirer)
FLP Scholar poster boy: Atty. Sean James Borja -- Ateneo valedictorian, numero uno in 2018 bar exam
Wisdom for scholars: bar topnotchers → top corporate executives or private entrepreneurs → marriage → children → passing the baton to the next generation

Life as a strange interplay of light and shadows -- CJP's personal narrative: UP scholarship closed by 15-centavo bus fare; FEU opened larger window via Salonga; Yale scholarship (full, with board and lodging) closed by US Embassy visa denial due to student activism; each closed door opened wider windows
1,200+ fully signed decisions in 11 years; one book per year; chairman of most SC committees; 'Renaissance Jurist of the 21st Century' resolution

At 75, inspired by 'Ageless Passion' (Ryan Cayabyab), transformed philosophy from 'imbedded legal lore' to 'practical reality' through organizing FLP; seeded with P2 million; companies and foundations contributed P50+ million for 700-sqm head office in Salcedo Village, Makati; another P50 million for educational projects

Museum for Liberty and Prosperity: interactive (visitors immerse inside virtual SC Session Hall, see oral arguments, ask questions); AI-powered (robots mimicking justices filled with decisions, speeches, bio data); plans being finalized by FLP Task Force headed by retired SAJ Estela Perlas-Bernabe; partnership with Supreme Court
Prosperity Fund: multi-billion peso, nonprofit but financially viable, to nurture and grow MSMEs; planned by FLP Task Force headed by Gov. Tetangco

Seed donation: family's Paseo de Magallanes, Makati residential lot worth P100M+ donated to FLP last year; to be liquified as seed money; 23 million pesos already contributed by friends for the two ultimate projects
Matthew 25:40: 'Whatever you do for the least of my brethren, you do unto me' as the theological foundation for the Prosperity Fund

stances.claim: Every closed door opens a wider window -- CJP's own life proves it: poverty blocked the UP scholarship (15-centavo bus fare), but FEU opened the larger window via Salonga; the US Embassy refused a Yale visa (due to student activism), but hard-knock education opened wider windows. This is the governing wisdom CJP delivers to the scholars.
stances.rhetorical_move: closed-door-open-window autobiography as prescriptive life philosophy for the scholars

stances.claim: The Museum for Liberty and Prosperity is not a passive repository but an active immersive experience: visitors are transported inside a virtual Supreme Court Session Hall, see and hear oral arguments, ask questions, and interact with AI robots mimicking justices filled with their decisions, speeches, and biographical data.
stances.rhetorical_move: immersion-design argument: the museum is an active civic education tool, not a trophy case

stances.claim: The Prosperity Fund is the institutional bridge between CJP's judicial philosophy (liberty under the rule of law) and the real-life problem of extreme poverty: 'liberty and prosperity must always be together -- one is useless without the other'; 'freedom must be of the mind and of the stomach; food must be of the intellect and of the gut.'
stances.rhetorical_move: dyadic-inseparability argument: the two beacons collapse into meaninglessness without each other

stances.claim: Ryan Cayabyab's musical 'Ageless Passion' was the inspirational trigger that at age 75 moved CJP from mere judicial philosophy to institutional action -- from 'imbedded legal lore' to 'practical reality' through the FLP.
stances.rhetorical_move: artistic-inspiration-as-institutional-trigger: a musical work as the catalyst for civic foundation-building

notable_anecdotes: Injap Sia's P888,000 unsolicited donation: declined to attend due to a prior commitment but 'instead sent an unsolicited donation of P888,000! Palakpakan po natin si Injap.'

The 15-centavo door: CJP won a UP scholarship but his impoverished family could not afford the then-measly 15-centavo ride to Diliman. He enrolled at nearby FEU instead, where he met his lifelong mentor Salonga.

The Yale visa denial: granted a full scholarship (including board and lodging) to Yale but refused a US Embassy visa because of his student activism. The wider window: 'a wider window of hard knock education opened.'

Msgr. Gerry Santos as 'Nak': CJP calls Msgr. Gerry 'Nak' (son); Msgr. calls CJP 'Tay' (father) and the late Leni 'Nay' (mother) -- a touching familial register, delivered just three months after Leni's death.

Felipe Gozon story: 'When I was still an incumbent in the Supreme Court, I invited Henry, who was, and still is, one of the best law practitioners of our country, to join the Court, but he preferred to stay as the GMA boss and made it unquestionably the largest TV-radio conglomerate in the Philippines.' CJP has sat as GMA independent director for 16 years since retiring in 2006.

Museum immersion example: 'visitors can be transported or immersed inside a virtual Session Hall of the Supreme Court where they can see and hear oral arguments, ask oral questions, and give stimulating comments.' AI robots mimicking justices filled with decisions, speeches, and bio data.
Sean James Borja as FLP poster boy: Ateneo valedictorian, numero uno in the 2018 bar exam -- the first in a tradition of bar topnotchers CJP expects all scholars to continue.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered July 28, 2023 at the FLP Awards Ceremony welcoming 21 new law scholars, 10 dissertation winners, and 5 ESMEL fellows, this speech by CJP opens by thanking CJ Gesmundo (keynote and Legal Scholarship Board of Judges chair), Kyle Tan (Tan Yan Kee Foundation, grandson of Dr. Lucio C. Tan), Fernando Zobel de Ayala (Ayala Corporation), Alfred and Cherry Ty (Metrobank Foundation), Msgr. Gerry Santos ('Nak' to CJP's 'Tay' and the late Leni's 'Nay' -- three months after Leni's April 9, 2023 death), Justice Amy Lazaro-Javier, Gov. Tetangco (SM Investments Chair, first P1-trillion-cap company), Atty. Felipe Gozon (GMA -- whom CJP once invited to join the Court), World Bank executives Dandan Chen and Dave Llorito, Injap Sia (absent but donated an unsolicited P888,000 -- 'Palakpakan po natin si Injap'), and Marixi Rufino Prieto (donated a colored Inquirer ad). He presents wisdom to the scholars through his life narrative: poverty blocked his UP scholarship (15-centavo bus fare), but FEU opened the window to Salonga; a Yale scholarship was blocked by a US Embassy visa denial (due to student activism), but hard-knock education followed; each closed door opened a wider window. He also recounts producing 1,200+ decisions and one book per year at the Court, earning the unanimous 'Renaissance Jurist' resolution, before being inspired at age 75 by Cayabyab's 'Ageless Passion' to transform judicial philosophy from 'imbedded legal lore' to 'practical reality' by organizing FLP (seeded with P2 million, now over P50 million in head office and P50 million in educational projects). He unveils FLP's two ultimate projects: the immersive, AI-powered Museum for Liberty and Prosperity (visitors inside a virtual SC Session Hall; AI robots mimicking justices; Task Force headed by retired SAJ Perlas-Bernabe) and the multi-billion-peso Prosperity Fund for MSMEs (Task Force headed by Gov. Tetangco). The family's P100M+ Paseo de Magallanes lot is donated as seed money; 23 million pesos already pledged by friends. He closes: 'Liberty and prosperity must always be together -- freedom must be of the mind and of the stomach... food must be of the intellect and of the gut' and invokes Matthew 25:40 ('Whatever you do for the least of my brethren, you do unto me') as the divine mandate for the Prosperity Fund.
